audit.whatIsWrong: Chart reads Akshan / Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Akshan, but the prose says level 1 is even and 'from level 2 onward you take over', and the packet chart reads Skill then Urgot on every remaining row.
audit.why: 51.21% over 908 games with a page that describes Urgot taking over from level 2 cannot show five neutral rows and two Akshan rows. The one genuinely even stage is Level 1, where his ranged Avengerang trades against Urgot's base kit.
audit.corrected: Skill / Urgot / Urgot / Urgot / Urgot / Urgot / Urgot, proposed as one group with the win[N] pairs and ratings. Difficulty also pulled from 7/10 to 5/10 to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page names Heroic Swing as the matchup-defining cooldown but never gives its number, and never mentions that it needs terrain to hook.
audit.why: Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1 and Riot's text says he is knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain — that is the whole reason the engage window exists.
audit.corrected: 18s, the terrain requirement and the champion-collision knock-off written into spikes[0] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and whys[4] call Comeuppance 'a channel that reveals him' and tell you to beat it at range; spikes[2] credits Corrosive Charge with shred it does not have; Going Rogue's camouflage is never mentioned despite there being no reveal in Urgot's kit.
audit.why: Riot's Comeuppance text describes a lock-on and stored bullets scaling with missing health, with no reveal stated — and both ultimates are 2500 range, so no one out-ranges anyone. Corrosive Charge does physical damage and a slow. Going Rogue is camouflage, so Control Wards and a sweeper are the only answer.
audit.corrected: Range parity and the missing-health scaling stated, the reveal claim dropped rather than reversed, Q described as slow not shred, and the camouflage vision requirement written into spikes[3].

edits.before: At 2 your Q lets you shred and answer his poke, tipping it to you.
edits.after: At 2 your Q slow answers his poke and tips the level to you.

edits.before: At 6 your R execute beats his revealing R channel.
edits.after: At 6 both Rs reach 2500 — win the threshold race.

edits.before: Once you have Q and E, close the gap: Akshan's damage is his Avengerang (Q) and passive double-hit, but he has no escape besides E grapple onto terrain, so E him off his swing path and W-shred him through his passive shield.
edits.after: Once you have Q and E, close the gap: his only escape is Heroic Swing, 18s at rank 1 and it needs terrain to hook — champion collision knocks him off it, so stand in the swing path and W-shred through his shield.

edits.before: His R Comeuppance is a long-range execute-scaling shot but it's a channel that reveals him, so at 6 you can R Fear Beyond Death him mid-channel or simply walk him down while he can't kite through your W slow.
edits.after: Comeuppance scales off your missing health and reaches 2500 — exactly your own R's range, so the race goes to whoever is nearer their threshold. Stay topped up, then Fear Beyond Death him while he stores bullets.

edits.before: With one item and boots you out-tank his poke; keep Corrosive Charge on him as he Qs so the shred plus your passive flames out-damage his ranged chip before he stacks his passive.
edits.after: With one item and boots you out-tank his poke; land Corrosive Charge as he throws Avengerang so the slow plus Echoing Flames beat his chip before his passive reaches three hits for the shield.

edits.before: Late Akshan wants to roam and pick, not sidelane you; if he does stand and fight, your HP and R execute beat him because his only defensive layer is the passive shield you shred straight through.
edits.after: Late Akshan roams rather than sidelane you, and Going Rogue is camouflage nothing in your kit reveals — Control Wards and a sweeper are mandatory. Stand-and-fight still favours your HP and R execute.

edits.before: - Akshan Heroic Swing: matchup-defining — His dash + camera swing escape. Engage when it's down. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Akshan Heroic Swing: matchup-defining — 18s at rank 1, needs terrain to hook, and champion collision knocks him off. Engage when it is down.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 7/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Heroic Swing and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Heroic Swing and how disciplined your pattern is.

edits.before: Tricky matchup — difficulty 7/10, Akshan carry threat 8/10.
edits.after: Tricky matchup — difficulty 5/10, Akshan carry threat 8/10.

notes: champ-data/_kits/_missing/urgot.json carries a 'dash-denied' claim that Akshan's Going Rogue and Heroic Swing deny Corrosive Charge as a dash. Corrosive Charge is a ranged explosive charge, not a dash — the 'dash' flag on Urgot's Q is a tooltip-parse misfire against Riot's own description. Not written to the page. The reveal-on-Comeuppance claim was removed rather than reversed: Riot's text neither confirms nor denies it.
